change_summary: EXP-579 inserted a navigational "Guide for skimmers" paragraph into the Part 2 intro (before the §2.1 details block) pointing skimmers to §2.9 (V13 coordinate circularity) as the foundational self-contradiction and §2.1 (Schumann) as the most numerically closed.
our_argument_summary: The signpost paragraph makes two characterizations: (1) §2.9 V13 coordinate system is circular — converts globe positions to dome coordinates then checks against the globe distances it started from, so any good fit is guaranteed; (2) §2.1 Schumann is the most numerically closed — H(r)=8,537·exp(-r/8,619) forces the resonant frequency to ≈22 Hz "at every radius" with no free parameter to reach the observed 7.83 Hz.

holes_found.description: The signpost says §2.1 "forces the resonant frequency to ≈22 Hz at every radius." This is factually wrong and contradicts §2.1’s own central argument. §2.1 explicitly argues f_QW(r) is MONOTONIC: it is at minimum ≈8.77 Hz at the pole and RISES outward — it is not constant at any value. The ≈22 Hz figure is specifically the linear radial AVERAGE (H_eff≈3,316 km → f≈22.6 Hz), one of several averaging schemes the section lists (polar 8.77 Hz, linear-radial-avg 22.6 Hz, area-weighted 35 Hz). A reader who sees "≈22 Hz at every radius" in the intro and then opens §2.1 ("minimum 8.77 Hz at the pole and rises monotonically from there") meets a direct internal contradiction — exactly the kind of inconsistency a dome defender exploits. Because the paragraph is reader-visible intro prose before any section is expanded, the error is seen first.
holes_found.recommendation: Replace "forces the resonant frequency to ≈22 Hz at every radius" with language that matches §2.1’s monotonicity/supremum argument, e.g.: "forces the resonant frequency to a hard floor of ≈8.77 Hz at the pole, rising monotonically outward — best-case spatial averages still land at 22–35 Hz — with no remaining free parameter able to reach the observed 7.83 Hz." This preserves the (correct) conclusion while removing the false "at every radius" constancy claim.

holes_found.description: The signpost foregrounds the ≈22 Hz linear-radial-average as the headline number for "most numerically closed," but §2.1 itself labels a DIFFERENT number its strongest argument: "The supremum impossibility (strongest argument)" — the ≈8.77 Hz polar floor, a hard mathematical bound (E[f(X)] ≤ sup f(X)) that no weighting scheme can evade. The 22 Hz value lives under §2.1’s own heading "Supplementary — rigorous averages (for reference)." Since the entire purpose of the signpost (per source hole HIER-PHASE2-07) is to route skimmers to the STRONGEST material, leading with a "for reference" average rather than the self-identified strongest argument partially defeats the navigational goal.
holes_found.recommendation: Lead the §2.1 pointer with the 8.77 Hz polar-floor supremum bound (the section’s self-labeled strongest argument), mentioning the 22–35 Hz averages as supporting detail. This also resolves Hole 0 in the same edit.

stronger_arguments.description: The signpost could note that §2.1’s impossibility is a SUPREMUM bound, not a calibration gap — the dome cannot reach 7.83 Hz at any radius or under any average, which is strictly stronger than "the numbers do not match." Framing it as "mathematically impossible given the dome’s own H(r)" is more durable than "≈22 Hz."

kernel_of_truth.description: The navigational intent is sound and well-grounded. The §2.9 characterization is accurate verbatim against the section (data/sections.json §2.9: "The formula is circular: it converts globe positions to dome coordinates, computes a ‘predicted’ distance, and compares it against the globe distance it started from"), and identifying §2.9 as the foundational self-contradiction matches the source hole HIER-PHASE2-07 (EXP-582-baby-batch-1.json: curmudgeon "explicitly named §2.9 as the foundation argument"). The H(r)=8,537·exp(-r/8,619) constant and the 7.83 Hz observed value both match §2.1 exactly (data/sections.json §2.1).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Accurate §2.9 framing does not excuse the §2.1 error: the same paragraph that correctly routes skimmers to §2.9 mis-states §2.1’s result as a constant ≈22 Hz ‘at every radius,’ directly contradicting §2.1’s monotonicity argument (data/sections.json §2.1: "at minimum 8.77 Hz at the pole and rises monotonically from there"). A signpost is only as trustworthy as its weakest pointer; the §2.1 pointer must be corrected before the paragraph is bulletproof.

deeper_analysis: EXP-579 is a verification-class navigational insert, but it embeds two substantive numerical characterizations and one of them is wrong in a way that creates an internal contradiction. §2.1’s structure is: (a) strongest argument = polar quarter-wave floor f_QW(0)=300000/(4·8537)≈8.77 Hz, monotonically rising; (b) supplementary ‘for reference’ averages = 22.6 Hz (linear radial) and 35 Hz (area-weighted). The signpost collapsed this into "≈22 Hz at every radius," which (i) picks the secondary number, and (ii) asserts constancy that §2.1 explicitly denies. The conclusion the signpost draws (no free parameter reaches 7.83 Hz) is correct and survives — this is a phrasing/number-selection error, not a verdict error, hence minor_edit and current_verdict_holds:true. Counter-view considered: one could argue 22 Hz is defensible because the section TITLE reads ‘7.83 Hz vs ~22 Hz,’ so the signpost merely echoes the title; but the title’s 22 Hz and the body’s 8.77-Hz ‘strongest argument’ are themselves in mild tension, and ‘at every radius’ has no support in either the title or the body. The fix is a single sentence and resolves both holes at once.
